newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Euro-MP demands inquiry into Channel Tunnel fire.
newsitem.headline: Euro-MP demands inquiry into Channel Tunnel fire.

text.p: A British Conservative Euro-MP called on Thursday for a European Commission inquiry into the Channel Tunnel goods train fire, following fears that the blaze may have been caused by sabotage.
"Parliament must...force the Commission to investigate incidents where travellers' lives are at risk," Anne McIntosh told the European Parliament.

"The Channel Tunnel is an essential link between the U.K. and the continent, where passengers must feel sure that travel is completely safe," McIntosh said during a debate on plans to improve EU transport infrastructure.
A fire in a lorry on the freight train seriously damaged a section of the tunnel on Monday last week, injuring 34 people and raising doubts about the safety of the cross-Channel service.
The Eurostar high-speed passenger train and Le Shuttle car and passenger services have been halted, although a limited freight service has resumed.
With EU countries planning to build other tunnels as part of a Europe-wide transport network, it was crucial to examine the safety aspects of Europe-wide travel, McIntosh said.
Channel Tunnel operator Eurotunnel sought on Wednesday to allay public fears about the risks of the rail link between Britain and France
"Safety is our first consideration, ahead of commercial considerations," Robert Malpas, the British Co-Chairman of the Anglo-French company told a news conference in Paris.
The cause of the fire remains a mystery, although sabotage is seen as one possibility by the French magistrate investigating the fire.
But legal sources said the idea that the fire was started deliberately was regarded as a remote possibility and not the most likely cause.
Eurotunnel hopes to resume partial passenger service early next week, if the safety commission that oversees the tunnel approves a new set of temporary evacuation measures.
